- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 70+), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day low.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.00/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
